transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to lock the wrap disposition plan today. As we all know, the set is scheduled for dismantling on Friday after the final stage shoot. The current draft plan sends scenic pieces to a general salvage vendor and places selected hero props in production storage. Before I can approve this plan, I need each department lead to confirm the exact disposition and environmental-compliance requirements for their department. If anyone has an exception to the draft plan, please state the exact corrective requirement now so it can be entered into the meeting record. Let's go through this systematically.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan. The antique jukebox listed as a hero prop is actually a rental, and its agreement requires it to be returned to the owner in its original condition rather than being placed in production storage or sent to salvage. I confirmed this with the rental house yesterday but had not yet entered it into the wrap packet. The corrective requirement is: remove the antique jukebox from the hero props designated for production storage and instead schedule its return to the rental house owner in its original condition before the Friday dismantling.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan. The production's city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill, and the approved vendor's audited plan reaches that threshold only through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. I confirmed the plan with the vendor this morning, but the compliance packet still contains the general-salvage draft. The corrective requirement is: replace the general salvage vendor disposition for scenic pieces with the approved vendor's audited wood and metal recycling bin plan plus certified transfer record, and update the compliance packet accordingly before the Friday dismantling.
